description: Trigger evals for image-to-spec: it fires when the only source is a screenshot, mockup, or gameplay capture and a structured spec is wanted, while component-spec, screen-spec, implement-approved-slice, journey-map and pattern-doc handle Figma-backed specs, code, multi-screen flows, and reusable patterns.

should_trigger: I only have a PNG of the pricing card, no Figma file. Can you write up a spec for it?

The designer sent a JPG mockup of the settings page (settings-v2.jpg in the assets folder) and there is nothing in Figma yet. Turn it into a screen spec with the copy quoted exactly so we can hand it to i18n.
Here is a screenshot of the login screen from the competitor app. Document the layout, spacing and components you can see, and flag anything you are only guessing.
I extracted twelve frames from a playtest video of the platformer plus my notes. Derive the rules of the jump and dash mechanics from them, marking what you actually saw versus what you assume.
grab this screenshot of the chip and describe it as a component doc, I'm not sure if it counts as a molecule

should_not_trigger.prompt: The designer finally put the pricing card into Figma (node 412:88), so we can stop working from the old screenshot. Document the card from the Figma node with its variants, states and tokens.
The checkout frame is already in Figma. Pull it with the design tools and produce the screen spec with layout and copy.
Take this screenshot of the profile screen and build it in React Native, the plan is approved and slice 02 covers it.

I have screenshots of all six onboarding screens in order and the user story. I don't need each screen written up on its own, I need the flow between them: what the user is trying to finish, which components each step uses, and the critical states along the way.

I collected screenshots of how five different apps handle pull to refresh. I don't want a spec of any one of them. I want our own reusable pull to refresh pattern that every product we build can follow.
